Let \(n\) be an integer that is either even with \(n\ge 10\) or odd with \(n\ge 15\). Let \(\mathcal R_n\) be the class of finite connected simple undirected graphs on \(n\) vertices in which all vertices have the same degree; this common degree may vary between graphs in \(\mathcal R_n\). Here simple means that loops and multiple edges are forbidden.

For \(G\in\mathcal R_n\), let \((X_k)_{k\ge0}\) be the discrete-time random walk that moves at each step to a uniformly chosen neighbor of its current vertex. For \(v\in V(G)\), set
\[
T_v=\inf\{k\ge0:X_k=v\},
\]
and let \(\mathbb E_u\) denote expectation when \(X_0=u\). Define
\[
\tau(G)=\max_{u,v\in V(G)}\bigl(\mathbb E_uT_v+\mathbb E_vT_u\bigr),
\qquad
 t_n=\max_{G\in\mathcal R_n}\tau(G).
\]
Determine an explicit exact formula for \(t_n\) as a function of \(n\) throughout the stated domain.

    pairs=list(combinations(range(n),2));S=0;commutes=[];count=0
    for mask in range(1<<N):
        G=nx.Graph();G.add_nodes_from(range(n))
        G.add_edges_from(e for j,e in enumerate(pairs) if (mask>>j)&1)
        ds=[G.degree(i) for i in range(n)]
        L=sp.Matrix([[ds[i] if i==j else -int(G.has_edge(i,j))
                      for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)])
        K=int(L[:n-1,:n-1].det())
        q=1-int(sp.floor(sp.Rational(1,K+1)))
        r=math.prod(int(sp.floor(sp.Rational(1,1+(d-ds[0])**2))) for d in ds[1:])

        F=int(L.extract(list(range(2,n)),list(range(2,n))).det())

## Formula

Put
\[
N=\binom n2,\qquad H=n^{\,n-2},\qquad
D=\operatorname{lcm}(1,2,\ldots,H),\qquad b=N+1,
\]
and define, for integers \(z\),
\[
\delta(z)=\left\lfloor\frac1{1+z^2}\right\rfloor.
\]
Thus \(\delta(z)=1\) exactly when \(z=0\).

Number the pairs \(1\le i<j\le n\) lexicographically, starting at zero:
\[
r(i,j)=\frac{(i-1)(2n-i)}2+j-i-1.
\]
For each integer \(0\le m<2^N\), define a symmetric matrix \(A_m=(a_{ij})\) by
\[
a_{ii}=0,\qquad
a_{ij}=a_{ji}
=\left\lfloor\frac{m}{2^{r(i,j)}}\right\rfloor
-2\left\lfloor\frac{m}{2^{r(i,j)+1}}\right\rfloor
\quad(i<j).
\]
Define
\[
d_i=\sum_j a_{ij},\qquad
L_m=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)-A_m.
\]
The \(d_i\) below depend on \(m\). Let
\[
K_m=\det L_m[\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\{2\}],
\qquad
F_m=\det L_m[\{3,\ldots,n\}],
\]
where brackets denote a principal submatrix.

Finally, set
\[
w_m=
\bigl(1-\delta(K_m)\bigr)
\prod_{i=2}^n\delta(d_i-d_1),
\qquad
e_m=\frac{Dnd_1F_m}{K_m+\delta(K_m)}
\]
and
\[
S_n=\sum_{m=0}^{2^N-1}w_m\,2^{\,b e_m}.
\]

Then the following is an explicit exact formula answering the question:
\[
\boxed{\displaystyle
t_n=\frac1D
\left\lfloor\frac{\log_2 S_n}{\binom n2+1}\right\rfloor .}
\tag{1}
\]
All the quantities on the right are specified directly by \(n\), with finite bounds. In particular, the right side contains no graph optimization, hitting times, unspecified constants, or recurrences. Each \(e_m\) is a nonnegative integer, as proved below.

In fact, (1) holds for every \(n\ge2\), so it covers the entire requested domain.

### 1. The flags select exactly the required matrices

Every \(A_m\) is the adjacency matrix of a labelled simple graph, and every such matrix occurs exactly once.

By the matrix-tree theorem, \(K_m\) is its number of spanning trees. Consequently,
\[
K_m>0\iff A_m\text{ represents a connected graph}.
\]
Also,
\[
0\le K_m\le n^{n-2}=H,
\tag{2}

\begin{cases}
1,&A_m\text{ represents a connected regular graph},\\
